notes: Community pack, roadmap Phase 1 candidate. 5 tracks x 10 themes x 5 grade bands = 250 blocks. Expanded by tools/generate_pack.py.

tracks.name: Moving through the city without a car

themes.description: Lines, interchanges and frequency — a transit map as a graph of what is actually reachable, and what the map exaggerates.
themes.transfer_check: Plan and complete (or fully paper-run) a three-leg journey on a real network using only its map and timetable.

bands.K–2: Point at your stop on a simple bus map, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Find a real route on a real transit map, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Read a real network map to plan a real trip, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real trip using a real network map on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to read a real transit network map confidently.

themes.theme: Fares, passes and the cheapest way in
themes.description: Singles, caps, passes and concessions — pricing a month of real travel and the discounts people never claim.
themes.transfer_check: Price one month of your actual journeys three ways and identify the cheapest legitimate option, including any concession you qualify for.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how much a bus or train ride costs.
bands.3–5: Learn about a real fare or pass option, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Compare real fare options to find the cheapest way in, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Choose the real cheapest fare option for your own real travel, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on the real cheapest way to pay for transit.

themes.description: Scheduled versus real service, live trackers, and building the buffer that makes you on time without waiting your life away.
themes.transfer_check: Compare scheduled and actual arrivals for one route across five observations and derive the buffer you would actually use.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if the bus always comes exactly on time.
bands.3–5: Learn that a real timetable is a guide, not a guarantee, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Compare a real timetable to real actual service, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real trip accounting for real timetable unreliability, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real gap between a timetable and reality.

themes.description: The gap between the stop and the door — walking routes, shared bikes and scooters, and judging each option's real cost and risk.
themes.transfer_check: Solve one real last-mile problem two different ways and compare them on time, cost and safety.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how you get from the bus stop to your door.
bands.3–5: Learn what the real 'last mile' of a trip means, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Plan a real solution for the real last mile of a journey, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan your own real last-mile solution for a real trip, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on solving the real last-mile problem for their trip.

themes.theme: Travelling with wheels, bags and small people
themes.description: Buggies, luggage, wheelchairs and toddlers on transit — the accessible routes, the boarding rules and the etiquette that matters.
themes.transfer_check: Plan a fully step-free journey on a real network for a named passenger with a mobility constraint, verifying each link's accessibility.

bands.K–2: Help carry something on a bus trip, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn how to manage bags on a real transit trip, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real trip with extra gear like bags or a stroller, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage a real complex trip with wheels, bags or children, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on travelling with real extra gear or dependents.

themes.theme: Night travel and the safety calculus
themes.description: Late services, lit routes, staffed stations and the trade-offs people quietly make — planning night moves deliberately.
themes.transfer_check: Plan a late-night journey home from a real venue with a primary and a fallback, and state the safety reasoning for each choice.

bands.K–2: Stay close to an adult when travelling at night.
bands.3–5: Learn one safety tip for real travel after dark, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Assess a real night travel route for real safety, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan your own real night travel with a real safety calculation, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on the real safety calculus for travelling at night.

themes.description: Strikes, closures, stranded platforms — rerouting in the moment and knowing your rights to refunds and alternatives.
themes.transfer_check: Given a real or staged disruption, produce a reroute within ten minutes and file (or fully draft) the refund claim the rules allow.

bands.K–2: Stay with an adult if a bus doesn't come.
bands.3–5: Know one backup plan if real transit is disrupted, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real backup route when service is disrupted, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Handle a real service disruption on your own, with a backup plan.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to plan for a real transit service failure.

themes.theme: Intercity: coach, rail and the booking game
themes.description: Advance fares, split tickets, railcards and the hour when prices change — long-distance travel bought well.
themes.transfer_check: Price one real intercity trip three ways at two booking horizons and document the cheapest defensible combination.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how you'd travel to a faraway city.
bands.3–5: Learn about a real coach or train option between cities, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Compare real intercity travel options and booking strategies, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Book a real intercity trip strategically for the best price, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on the real booking game for intercity travel.

themes.description: When a cab is the right tool, estimating a fare before riding, surge pricing, and the licensed-versus-unlicensed line.
themes.transfer_check: Estimate a real taxi/rideshare fare before booking, compare the actual, and verify the vehicle and driver checks you should always make.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how a taxi charges for a ride.
bands.3–5: Learn how a real taxi or rideshare fare is calculated, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Compare a real taxi and rideshare fare for the same trip, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Choose the real most cost-effective option between taxi and rideshare, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how real taxi and rideshare pricing actually works.

themes.description: Time, money and energy across all modes — auditing how you actually move and redesigning the pattern on evidence.
themes.transfer_check: Log every journey for one week with time and cost, then redesign your default mode for one regular trip and trial it.

bands.K–2: Help count how much a family spends getting around, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help track real transport spending for a week, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Build a real personal mobility budget, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage your own real mobility budget across trip types, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on building a real workable personal mobility budget.

themes.description: Frame, drivetrain, brakes, contact points — naming the parts and knowing which failures stop a ride versus end one.
themes.transfer_check: Identify every major component on a real bike and classify five common faults as ride-on, fix-first or walk-home.

bands.K–2: Point at the wheels and pedals of a bike, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Name the real main parts of a real bicycle, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real bicycle's key parts and their function, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain how a real bicycle's parts work together, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real mechanics of how a bicycle actually works.

themes.description: The two-minute pre-ride inspection — brakes, wheels, headset, drivetrain — that catches most mechanical surprises.
themes.transfer_check: Perform a full M-check on a real bike, find the planted or genuine fault, and fix or flag it correctly.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult check a bike before riding.
bands.3–5: Check a real bike's tyres and brakes before riding, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Perform a real M-check on a bicycle before riding, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Perform a real full M-check on your own bike before every ride.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to perform a real M-check correctly.

themes.description: Removing a wheel, finding the cause, patching or replacing the tube, and getting the wheel back on straight.
themes.transfer_check: Repair a real puncture end to end, including finding what caused it, and ride the result.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult fix a flat bike tyre and ask questions.
bands.3–5: Learn one step of fixing a real flat tyre, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Fix a real flat bicycle tyre, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Fix a real flat bicycle tyre on your own, start to finish.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to fix a real flat tyre from start to finish.

themes.theme: Brakes and gears that actually work
themes.description: Cable tension, pad wear and indexing — the two adjustments that transform most neglected bikes.
themes.transfer_check: Adjust the brakes and index the gears on a real bike until both pass a named performance test.

bands.K–2: Squeeze the brakes on a bike gently, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Check that real brakes and gears work properly, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Adjust a real bicycle's brakes or gears, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Maintain your own real bicycle's brakes and gears, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to keep real brakes and gears working well.

themes.description: Road position, eye contact, the door zone and the left-turning lorry — the defensive craft of city cycling.
themes.transfer_check: Ride (or walk-and-narrate) a real urban route, calling out position choices and the two highest-risk conflict points.

bands.K–2: Ride a bike only where an adult says it's safe.
bands.3–5: Learn one real traffic safety rule for riding, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Ride a real bicycle safely in real traffic, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Ride a real bicycle safely and confidently in real traffic, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else safe, confident real riding technique in traffic.

themes.theme: Locks, theft and keeping the bike
themes.description: Lock types, locking technique, registration and where bikes actually get stolen — defence in depth for a parked bike.
themes.transfer_check: Lock a real bike correctly in a public rack, register its frame number, and critique three locking jobs you find nearby.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult lock up a bike properly and ask why.
bands.3–5: Learn one real way to lock a bike securely, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Lock a real bicycle securely against real theft, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Secure your own real bicycle properly every time, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real best practices to prevent bicycle theft.

themes.description: Racks, panniers, trailers and child seats — turning a bike into a vehicle that does errands.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a real shopping or school-run trip by bike with the load properly mounted, and report what worked and what shifted.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult carry something on a bike safely.
bands.3–5: Learn a real safe way to carry something on a bike, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Carry a real load safely on a bicycle, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Carry real cargo or a passenger safely on a bicycle, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to safely carry real cargo or passengers by bike.

themes.description: E-bikes and e-scooters: motors, range reality, charging safely (the battery fire problem), and the laws that differ by vehicle.
themes.transfer_check: For one real e-vehicle, state its legal class and rules where you live, and demonstrate or describe its safe charging setup.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how an electric bike is different.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real electric assist does on a bike, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Explain how a real e-bike's assist works, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real e-bike as an option for your own travel, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real trade-offs of an electric-assist bicycle.

themes.theme: Weather, night and the visible rider
themes.description: Lights, reflectives, rain technique and ice honesty — extending the riding year without extending the risk.
themes.transfer_check: Equip a real bike for legal, effective night riding and demonstrate the visibility difference from a driver's viewpoint.

bands.K–2: Wear bright colours when riding, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn one way to be seen while riding, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Prepare a real bicycle and rider to be visible in bad conditions, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare your own real bike and gear for weather and night riding, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to stay visible in real bad weather or night riding.

themes.description: What wears on a bike, the maintenance calendar, and the jobs worth paying a shop to do.
themes.transfer_check: Write and begin the twelve-month maintenance plan for a real bike, performing this month's items yourself.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult clean and oil a bike chain.
bands.3–5: Learn one real bike maintenance task, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Follow a real bicycle maintenance schedule, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Maintain your own real bicycle on a proper schedule, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else a real bicycle maintenance schedule that actually works.

tracks.name: The car: owning, running, letting go

themes.description: Depreciation, insurance, fuel, maintenance, parking — total cost of ownership versus the sticker that gets all the attention.
themes.transfer_check: Compute the honest annual cost of one real car (or a planned one) and its cost per kilometre against the alternatives.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if a car costs more than just the price tag.
bands.3–5: Learn one real hidden cost of owning a car, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real full cost of car ownership beyond the price, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Calculate a real full cost of owning a car, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real full cost of car ownership over time.

themes.description: History checks, the walk-around, the test drive script and the seller's silences — inspecting value instead of paint.
themes.transfer_check: Run a full pre-purchase inspection on a real used car (or an accompanied case), including its documented history, and deliver a buy/walk verdict.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what to check before buying a used toy.
bands.3–5: Learn one thing to check on a real used item before buying, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real red flag when buying a real used car, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real used car purchase carefully, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to buy a real used car without being taken advantage of.

themes.theme: The fluids and the five-minute check
themes.description: Oil, coolant, brake fluid, washer, tyres — the monthly bonnet-up routine that prevents the expensive surprise.
themes.transfer_check: Perform the complete fluid-and-tyre check on a real car and correct or top up at least one item found low.

bands.K–2: Watch an adult check the oil in a car and ask why.
bands.3–5: Learn one real fluid a car needs checked, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Perform a real five-minute fluid check on a car, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Perform a real five-minute fluid check on your own car, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to perform a real quick fluid check.

themes.theme: Tyres: the only part touching the road
themes.description: Pressure, tread, age and the legal limits — and what each says about how the car is being used.
themes.transfer_check: Measure pressure and tread on all tyres of a real car, adjust to specification, and judge each tyre's remaining life.

bands.K–2: Look at a car's tyres with an adult and ask why they matter.
bands.3–5: Learn one real thing to check about a tyre, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Check real tyre tread and pressure correctly, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Check and maintain real tyres on your own vehicle, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else why real tyres are the only part touching the road.

themes.theme: Warning lights and the sounds of trouble
themes.description: Which dashboard lights mean stop now, which mean soon, and describing a noise so a mechanic can hear it too.
themes.transfer_check: Classify ten real warning lights by urgency from the handbook, and write one fault description a garage could diagnose from.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what a light on the car dashboard means.
bands.3–5: Learn one real dashboard warning light, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real dashboard warning light and its meaning, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Diagnose a real warning light or sound and respond appropriately, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to interpret real warning lights and sounds.

themes.description: Getting quotes, understanding the invoice, declining the upsell and knowing fair prices for common jobs.
themes.transfer_check: Obtain two quotes for one real repair or service, compare them line by line, and negotiate or choose with reasons stated.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult who fixes a car when it breaks.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real mechanic does, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real trustworthy garage relationship's traits, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Build a real trustworthy relationship with a real garage, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on building a real good relationship with a garage.

themes.theme: Insurance, claims and the day it goes wrong
themes.description: Cover levels, excesses, the at-the-scene checklist and the claim that gets paid because the evidence was gathered.
themes.transfer_check: Rehearse the full collision-scene procedure — safety, photos, details, admissions avoided — and file a complete mock claim.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why every car needs insurance to drive.
bands.3–5: Learn what car insurance protects against, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify what a real insurance claim process involves, with a checker.
bands.9–10: File or understand a real insurance claim process, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through a real insurance claim after an accident.

themes.description: Where to stop, when to exit the vehicle, warning others and waiting safely — the breakdown as a safety event first.
themes.transfer_check: Walk through a staged breakdown on three road types and state the correct positioning, signals and calls for each.

bands.K–2: Stay in the car and wait for an adult if it breaks down.
bands.3–5: Learn one real safety step for a car breakdown, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Respond safely to a real car breakdown, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Handle a real car breakdown safely on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real safe procedure for a roadside breakdown.

themes.description: Car clubs, rentals and the borrowed car — insurance realities, damage walk-arounds and the deposits that vanish.
themes.transfer_check: Complete a real or mock rental including the documented walk-around, and identify the two contract clauses most likely to cost you.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if you can share a ride with a friend's family.
bands.3–5: Learn about a real way to share transportation, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Compare a real car-sharing or rental option to owning, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate real car-sharing or rental options for your own needs, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on the real trade-offs of sharing versus owning.

themes.description: The annual review: kilometres driven, cost per trip, and the honest comparison against a life with fewer or no cars.
themes.transfer_check: Run the keep/replace/sell analysis for one real household car with a year's actual usage data, and present the recommendation.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult if walking or biking could work instead of driving.
bands.3–5: Consider a real alternative to owning a car, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Evaluate whether a real car is actually needed for your situation, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Decide, using real evidence, whether you actually need a car, on your own.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on honestly evaluating whether they need a real car.

tracks.name: Roads shared: safety for every user

themes.description: Sightlines, parked-car screens, signal phases and the crossing choices that fail — pedestrian craft taken seriously at every age.
themes.transfer_check: Assess three real crossing points near a school or home, rank their risk with reasons, and demonstrate the safest use of the worst one.

bands.K–2: Look both ways before crossing with an adult.
bands.3–5: Cross a real street safely by looking both ways, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Cross a real street safely at a real intersection, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Cross real streets safely and confidently on your own, every time.
bands.11–12: Teach a younger child the real skill of crossing a street safely.

themes.description: Stopping distances, survival curves and why 30 versus 50 is the difference between an injury and a funeral.
themes.transfer_check: Compute stopping distances at three speeds for a real road and match each against its actual sightlines and crossings.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why cars go slower near a school.
bands.3–5: Learn that real speed changes how dangerous a crash is, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Explain the real relationship between speed and crash severity, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Explain, using real data, why speed matters so much for safety.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real physics behind speed and crash outcomes.

themes.theme: The blind spots of big vehicles
themes.description: Trucks, buses and the zones where a person disappears — positioning around large vehicles as a survival rule.
themes.transfer_check: From a parked large vehicle's driver seat (or accurate diagram), map its blind zones and demonstrate the safe positions around it.

bands.K–2: Stay where a truck driver can see you, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Learn that real big vehicles have blind spots, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real blind spot around a real large vehicle, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Position yourself safely around real large vehicles, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else about the real blind spots of large vehicles.

themes.theme: Distraction: the phone in the hand
themes.description: What attention actually is on the road, the seconds a glance costs at speed, and the norms shifting around it.
themes.transfer_check: Measure reaction-time degradation under distraction in a safe simulated task and translate the result into metres at road speed.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why looking at a phone while walking is risky.
bands.3–5: Learn that a real phone distracts from real road safety, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real risk of distraction near roads, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Avoid real distraction near roads on your own, every time.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real evidence on distraction and road risk.

themes.description: What each does to driving, the limits and the myths, and stopping an impaired person from driving without a fight.
themes.transfer_check: Rehearse and script the intervention that takes keys from an impaired driver, and state the legal limits and alternatives where you live.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult why some people shouldn't drive.
bands.3–5: Learn that being tired or unwell affects real driving, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real form of impairment that affects road safety, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Recognise real impairment in yourself or others before driving, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else the real evidence on impairment and road risk.

themes.description: Why children misjudge speed and distance, the walking-bus and the taught routines that build safe pedestrians.
themes.transfer_check: Design and walk a safe school route for a real child, teaching them its three decision points and testing their recall.

bands.K–2: Hold an adult's hand whenever you are near a real road.
bands.3–5: Follow a real road safety rule near traffic, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real risk to children near roads, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Model real safe behaviour near roads for a younger child, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to keep children safe near real roads.

themes.description: Restraints fitted right — the belt path, the helmet angle, the child seat stages — and the fittings that silently fail.
themes.transfer_check: Fit and verify one real restraint (child seat, helmet or belt) against its manual, and find the deliberate or genuine fitting error.

bands.K–2: Buckle your seatbelt every time, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Wear a real helmet or seatbelt correctly, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Use real safety equipment correctly every time, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Ensure real safety equipment is used correctly for yourself and others.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real correct use of seatbelts, helmets and child seats.

themes.description: Arriving at a road collision: scene safety, the call that gets the right response, and what to do and not do before help arrives.
themes.transfer_check: Run a full staged first-on-scene response — protect, assess, call, assist — narrating each decision in order.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult right away if you see an accident.
bands.3–5: Know to get an adult's help if you see a real accident, with their help.
bands.6–8: Identify the real first steps to take at a real accident scene, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Respond appropriately as real first on scene at an accident, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else the real correct steps to take as first on scene.

themes.description: Widths, corners, crossings and parking as decisions someone made — why some streets calm traffic and others invite it.
themes.transfer_check: Audit one real street for design-induced risk and propose two concrete changes with the evidence behind each.

bands.K–2: Notice a crosswalk painted on a road, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Notice a real street design feature meant for safety, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Read a real street's design for its safety features, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Evaluate a real street's design for its safety strengths and gaps, on your own.
bands.11–12: Explain to someone else how to read a real street's design for safety.

themes.description: Reporting hazards, the authority responsible, and the campaign that turns a dangerous junction into an agenda item.
themes.transfer_check: Report one real road hazard through the official channel and draft the follow-up escalation to the responsible authority.

bands.K–2: Tell an adult about a broken sidewalk or pothole.
bands.3–5: Report a real road hazard to an adult, with their help.
bands.6–8: Identify the real process for reporting a road hazard, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Report a real road hazard through the correct process, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through getting a real dangerous road fixed.

tracks.name: Journeys: planning, rights and the wider world

themes.description: Route, timing, fallbacks and the single sheet that holds a journey together when the phone dies.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the one-page plan for a real multi-leg journey — times, references, fallbacks, contacts — and travel (or simulate) from it alone.

bands.K–2: Help plan a family day out, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Help plan a real simple trip's steps, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Plan a real trip as a project with steps and a timeline, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Plan a real trip from start to finish as a project, on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to plan a real trip as a structured project.

themes.description: Passports, visas, validity windows and the checks that happen before the airport — paperwork as the first leg of the trip.
themes.transfer_check: For a real or chosen destination, compile the full document checklist for a named traveller and verify each item's validity dates.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what papers are needed to travel far away.
bands.3–5: Learn what a real travel document is used for, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Identify a real required document for a real type of travel, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Prepare your own real travel documents correctly, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through preparing the real documents needed to travel.

themes.description: Cards abroad, exchange margins, the ATM decline at midnight — and the backup layer that keeps a trip alive.
themes.transfer_check: Design the payment setup for a real trip — primary, backup, emergency cash — and state the fees each choice carries.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult how you pay for things on a trip.
bands.3–5: Learn one real way to manage money while travelling, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Plan real money management for a real trip, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Manage your own real money safely and efficiently while travelling.
bands.11–12: Advise someone else on real strategies for managing money on the move.

themes.description: Packing lists, weight limits and the things you cannot carry — travelling with everything needed and nothing dragged.
themes.transfer_check: Pack for a defined real trip within an airline's actual limits, justify every item, and pass a prohibited-items check.

bands.K–2: Help pack a small bag for a trip, with an adult.
bands.3–5: Pack a real bag for a real trip, with an adult's help.
bands.6–8: Pack real luggage efficiently for a real trip, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Pack real luggage efficiently and appropriately on your own.
bands.11–12: Teach someone else how to pack real luggage well for any trip.

themes.description: Compensation regimes, rerouting duties and the difference between what carriers owe and what they offer.
themes.transfer_check: For one real or case-study disruption, determine the passenger's actual entitlement under the applicable rules and draft the claim.

bands.K–2: Ask an adult what happens if a trip gets delayed.
bands.3–5: Learn that travellers have real rights when delayed, with an adult.
bands.6–8: Identify a real right you have during a real travel delay, with a checker.
bands.9–10: Assert your own real rights during a real delay or cancellation, on your own.
bands.11–12: Guide someone else through asserting real rights during travel disruption.
